study type: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
exposure: Intracervical Foley catheter with concurrent oxytocin infusion
cohort: Participants were patients with a live singleton pregnancy at >=24 weeks' gestation undergoing labor induction with a Foley catheter and an initial Bishop score of <=3.
finding: Concurrent Foley catheter and oxytocin infusion significantly reduced the time from induction to delivery in patients with a Bishop score of <=3 when compared with a Foley catheter only.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference in the rate of cesarean delivery between the groups.
